subsystems.name: Envelope
subsystems.role: holds helium at superpressure and resists sulfuric acid aerosols.

subsystems.name: Gondola
subsystems.role: carries instruments and avionics, suspended below the balloon.

subsystems.name: Altitude control
subsystems.role: maintains a stable float altitude or changes it using phase-change fluids or ballast.

subsystems.name: Power
subsystems.role: supplies electricity through the day-night cycle.

subsystems.name: Thermal control
subsystems.role: keeps electronics within operating temperature despite cold nights and hot days.

subsystems.name: Communications
subsystems.role: relays science data to an orbiter or directly to Earth.

buildSteps.title: Select and test envelope material
buildSteps.detail: Candidate polymer films are exposed to sulfuric acid aerosol, ultraviolet light and temperature cycling, then measured for strength and helium permeability.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the envelope
buildSteps.detail: Gores of film are cut and seam-sealed into a sphere, with load tapes attached to carry the gondola's weight.

buildSteps.title: Build the gondola
buildSteps.detail: Instruments, avionics, power and thermal systems are integrated and tested in a vacuum chamber.

buildSteps.title: Integrate balloon and payload
buildSteps.detail: The gondola is suspended below the envelope, connections for power and data are made, and the deployment sequence is rehearsed.

buildSteps.title: Earth flight testing
buildSteps.detail: Superpressure balloons are flown in the stratosphere to validate altitude stability and material performance.

buildSteps.title: Venus environment testing
buildSteps.detail: Chamber tests simulate Venus cloud conditions with sulfuric acid, pressure and temperature cycling.

buildSteps.title: Launch and cruise
buildSteps.detail: The packed aerobot is launched on a spacecraft and cruises to Venus.

buildSteps.title: Deploy and inflate
buildSteps.detail: After entry, a parachute or aeroshell slows the descent; the balloon inflates with helium and the gondola is released.

buildSteps.title: Operate and relay data
buildSteps.detail: The aerobot floats at about 55 km, conducts science, and sends data via an orbiter.

prerequisites.why: must survive sulfuric acid clouds for weeks; some polymers resist but need flight validation.
flown in Earth's stratosphere; provides stable altitude without ballast.
the 1985 Vega balloons deployed successfully but lasted only about two days.
solar power works in the cloud layer, but nights require batteries and insulation.
mass spectrometers and nephelometers exist, but need to be rugged and low-power for a balloon.
an orbiter can relay data from the balloon to Earth.

pathway.milestone: Earth analogue flights of superpressure balloons with acid-resistant materials for weeks in the stratosphere
pathway.unlocks: confidence in envelope durability and altitude control.

pathway.milestone: a small Venus balloon technology demonstration that floats for weeks and returns data
pathway.unlocks: proof of deployment, materials and communications at Venus.

pathway.milestone: a full aerobot mission with an instrument suite surveying the cloud layer for months
pathway.unlocks: detailed chemistry, including the unknown ultraviolet absorber.

pathway.milestone: multiple balloons or a balloon with a drone exploring different altitudes and latitudes
pathway.unlocks: a global picture of Venus's atmosphere and potential habitability.
